classification.rationale: The text is a transcript of an interview/podcast with Donald Hoffman discussing his theories on consciousness, spacetime, and simulation. It is media content featuring a key figure and philosophical/scientific topics, not a government document, witness testimony, or technical report.

_raw_list: Evolution has shaped sensory systems to guide adaptive behavior, not to see objective reality; the probability that we see reality as it is is precisely zero.
Spacetime is not fundamental; it is a headset or interface that hides the truth and provides only the controls needed for survival.
Objects in spacetime cease to exist when not perceived; they are rendered on the fly upon perception.
Local realism has been proved false (Nobel Prize), supporting the view that spacetime is not fundamental.
Consciousness is fundamental and not created by computational or neural processes; no theory explains even one specific conscious experience.
Simulation theories like Nick Bostrom's are flawed because they assume spacetime physics is fundamental and that computers can create consciousness.
Positive geometries (e.g., amplitudhedron, associahedron) are structures outside spacetime that may have billions of dimensions, indicating our spacetime is a low-dimensional projection.

claims_hint: Evolution shapes sensory systems for adaptive behavior, not objective truth.
Probability is precisely zero that evolution shaped us to see reality as it is.
SpaceTime is not fundamental; it is a headset or interface.
Local realism is false, supported by Nobel Prize.
Quantum states are degrees of subjective belief (QBism).
Positive geometries like amplitudhedron may have billions of dimensions.
Simulation theory (Bostrom) assumes physicalism and computational consciousness, both false.
No computational theory explains even one specific conscious experience.
Neurons are a headset projection; neuroscience needs to reverse engineer deeper reality.
Panpsychism (as described) ties consciousness to particles of the standard model, which is problematic.
